reason: The text demonstrates extensive expression of views by multiple characters. The sailors question Jonah and discuss their situation (וַיִּקְרְא֨וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־ אֱלֹהָיו). Jonah explicitly identifies himself and his faith to the sailors (עִבְרִ֣י אָנֹ֑כִי וְאֶת־ יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙). Jonah proclaims God's message to Nineveh without restriction. Most significantly, Jonah directly expresses his anger and theological complaint to God in detailed prayer (וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֨ל אֶל־ יְהוָ֜ה וַיֹּאמַ֗ר), and God engages him in dialogue, asking him questions about his anger. The entire narrative structure emphasizes dialogue and the voicing of concerns, complaints, and beliefs by its characters.
